The division adds its own severe layer: Feb 2026 law confining trans people to birth-sex facilities in public buildings incl. airports, government offices, schools, with civil and criminal penalties up to $1,000 and bounty-hunter private suits of at least $1,000 for sharing a bathroom with a trans person; bars updating DL/state IDs, invalidates existing licences with inconsistent markers, reissue at holder's expense. That's below the parent average: a documented territory-specific hostile layer on top of the parent's regime, and per rule 12, cannot score at or above parent average.

Note there is a state anti-discrimination law (public accommodations since 2020), hate crime law covers sexual orientation but not gender identity; marriage equality; but these are resident-facing climate signals mostly, and the operative harsh rule governs.

Compare to anchors: 0.15 anchors are severe risk: criminalised presentation with police sweeps, custody sexual assault, militia. Here: the bounty mechanism means any private person can sue — that's a continuous universal-exposure enforcement mechanism reaching every trans visitor using a public building including airports. Plus ID invalidation and possible driving penalties. Plus parent regime: border document scrutiny, possible refusal/entry issues, detention harm.

But it's not a presentation criminal offence with street sweeps. There is criminal penalty up to $1,000 (fine, not imprisonment) for facility use. Arrest occurred elsewhere under a trespass law. The police aren't documented as conducting sweeps against trans people here. Violence documentation is thin.

Where does this sit? The below-0.20 band is severe risk: near-certain imprisonment, organised targeting, or unremedied tier-1 with severe penalties. Here we have universal-exposure state-imposed facility exclusion with private bounty enforcement and ID invalidation, plus a hostile national border/detention regime with documented harm. That is roughly comparable to the 0.15-C / 0.25-A tier? Let me think. 0.25 anchors: police raids, extortion, birth-sex custody with abuse, dress-offence enforcement. 0.15 anchors: criminalisation of presentation with sweeps and imprisonment, militia targeting.

This division: no presentation criminal offence per se, but a bounty/private-lawsuit regime for bathroom use — that is effectively a universal exposure with civil and criminal penalty and private enforcement, in all publicly owned buildings including airports (which every air traveller passes through). Combined with the national regime: passport/visa refusal risk, fraud ineligibility ground, detention conditions documented as abusive (conversion therapy for inmates, forced labour, sexual abuse in immigration custody). Also national counterterrorism strategy rhetoric framing "radically pro-transgender" groups.

That's a serious combination — state-imposed universal exposure (tier 1) plus documented custodial harm plus hostile border regime. I'd put it around 0.15–0.20. The division's own layer is harsher than the national average, and the national average itself is quite low. Rule 12 says territory must sit materially below comparable independent jurisdictions lacking the regime; below parent's own average.

The parent regime is not fully at 0.15 — the national picture includes functioning courts that have sometimes enjoined, hate crime statute covering gender identity nationally, employment protection, marriage equality, 66% support for birth-sex documents (hostile), a mix. But the visitor-facing exposures: passport marker restrictions with confiscation/stranding, entry refusal risk, custody harm documented. Parent average maybe ~0.25-0.30. This division adds its own bounty law → materially below, ~0.15.

Also airports: this division's law covers airports, so transiting through an airport in this division triggers the facility rule and bounty exposure — a universal exposure every traveller faces.

I'll rate 0.15. Justification: worst documented feature is tier 1 state-imposed universal exposure (facility exclusion by birth sex in all public buildings, criminal/civil penalties, private bounty enforcement), plus ID invalidation, atop a parent regime with documented border exclusion, fraud-based lifetime ineligibility risk, and custodial abuse. Mitigating: no general presentation criminalisation, anti-discrimination law, functioning courts (though liability clause applies — courts upheld marker changes), pending lawsuit. Some room above 0.05 because the enforcement is fine-based and bounty-based rather than imprisonment/execution campaigns with near-certain prosecution.

Maybe 0.16-0.18. I'll say 0.17.
